name: Books & Bricks Cafe
why_it_matters: Opened in 2015 by childhood friends Danish Zargar and Arsalan Sajad — Srinagar's first reading-room style cafe. Varnished-brick interiors, walls papered with Reader's Digest pages, low bookshelves. Credited in TheBetterIndia and Slurrp coverage as the cafe that pulled Srinagar's youth out of hotel coffee shops and into independent cafes.
insider_tip: Books here are for reading on the premises, not for sale — pick one off the shelf when you order. The fish fillet burger, not the coffee, is what regulars come back for.
signature_address: Gogjibagh, Opposite Amar Singh College, Srinagar 190008

name: Cafè Liberty
why_it_matters: Retro-styled cafe on M.A. Road — the walls are a curated collection of antique radios, vintage skis, old Bollywood film posters and clocks. The walnut tart is widely cited as the best in Kashmir; the kitchen also serves a competent Kashmiri menu, which is unusual for a cafe at this price point.
insider_tip: Get there before 7pm if you want a window booth — Liberty fills up fast on weekends, and the Alijan Shopping Complex entrance is easy to miss (look for the side stairs).
signature_address: 309, Alijan Shopping Complex, M.A. Road, Lal Chowk, Srinagar 190001

name: 14th Avenue Cafe Grill & Bakeshop
why_it_matters: Family-run since 2012 from a single Lal Mandi outlet beside the footbridge over the Jhelum, now eight branches across Srinagar. Glass-walled river-view dining downstairs, a working bakeshop counter at the front — pastries, pies, savouries baked through the day. The cafe locals send tourists to when they want 'reliable, not touristy'.
insider_tip: The Lal Mandi flagship has the best Jhelum view and the freshest bake counter — other branches share the kitchen but not the river. Pick up a chocolate truffle for the houseboat back.
signature_address: Lal Mandi, near footbridge, Rajbagh, Srinagar 190008

name: Coffea Arabica
why_it_matters: Originally Srinagar's only proper espresso bar in the 90s and 2000s, Coffea Arabica was washed out in the 2014 floods and rebuilt as an extension of the Hotel Broadway — exposed brick, vintage clocks, dark-wood arches. Multi-cuisine menu now spans Mediterranean and Awadhi, but it remains one of the few spots in Srinagar where the espresso machine is taken seriously.
insider_tip: It's part of Hotel Broadway but open to walk-ins — enter via the Maulana Azad Road side entrance, not through hotel reception. Quietest 4-6pm; loud and student-heavy after 7pm.
signature_address: Hotel Broadway, Maulana Azad Road, near Kashmir Golf Course, Srinagar 190001

name: Goodfellas
why_it_matters: Cafe-cum-arts-space on the Bund opposite Jehlum Park — hosts art shows, gaming nights, story sessions and poetry slams in addition to standard service. Profiled by TheBetterIndia as one of the cafes redefining Srinagar's youth culture post-2010. Italian, Mexican and American mains alongside home-baked pastries and nun chai.
insider_tip: Check their Facebook page before your visit — events are weekly and many of the best evenings have an open-mic or screening. Outdoor terrace has Jhelum-side seating in summer.
signature_address: Near Mughal Darbar, opposite Jehlum Park, Residency Road, Srinagar 190001

name: Cafe Robusta Lounge
why_it_matters: One of Srinagar's earliest specialty-coffee outlets — operating since 2007 in the Polo Plaza shopping arcade. Quiet, no theme, no Instagram murals; the espresso machine and the bean is the point. Loyal regulars treat it as the city's unfussy coffee bar.
insider_tip: The first-floor lounge is calmer than the ground-floor takeaway counter; ask the barista for the day's roast — they switch beans seasonally and rarely write it on the menu.
signature_address: 1st Floor, Polo Plaza, Main Chowk, Polo View, Srinagar 190001

name: Crème by Ahdoos
why_it_matters: Ahdoos opened on Residency Road in 1918 and turned 100 in 2018, when the bakery half rebranded as Crème — the Ahdoos restaurant continues upstairs, the bakery-cafe runs at street level. The single most-cited spot for Kashmiri bakerkhani and sheermal in Srinagar's central zone.
insider_tip: Take a box of bakerkhani for the houseboat — they're best within four hours of baking, before the layered ghee resolidifies. The first batch comes out around 8am.

name: Shakti Sweets
why_it_matters: Founded in 1966 by Mengha Ram Sokhal, three generations on — the city-centre sweet shop that survived insurgency, curfews and the 2014 floods without closing. Pure-veg, snack counter at the front, sit-down bakery section behind. Default stop for North-Indian-style mithai in Lal Chowk.
insider_tip: The samosa-and-aloo-tikki counter at the entrance is heavier traffic than the sweets — the milk cake at the back display is what's worth queueing for. Boxes are vacuum-packed for travel on request.
signature_address: Residency Road, Regal Chowk, Lal Chowk, Srinagar 190001
